Past the stop the three azimuths show a diffuse light-blue spray, not an amber band, running forward about 11 cm at a visible kink: 54008 (7 pts, 3.6 cm, d_min 0.0 to 3.46, cos_fwd 0.89, 6.5e4 e/cm) then 54004 (15 pts, 8.5 cm, 3.46 to 10.92 cm, cos_fwd 0.79, 5.2e4 e/cm). Both sit at 1.0-1.2 times the local MIP plateau, and a muon that has just delivered 1.42e5 at its Bragg peak cannot carry on at MIP for another 11 cm, so the spray is a second particle: 11 cm at MIP is the right range for a ~25 MeV Michel, and inside 10 cm of the stop the rubric says direction does not discriminate anyway. I tagged 54008 michel even though the chain groups it with the muon and types it pdg 13, on the grounds that it lies past the charge maximum; I explicitly weighed the undershoot reading (that 54008 is the muon last 3.5 cm and the fit stopped short) and rejected it because the undershoot requires the tip to carry 0.9-1.2e5, several times MIP, and 6.5e4 is not that, while the 1.42e5 peak is behind the pin, not in the tip. 146006 is a 5-point, 2.4 cm, 8.8e3 e/cm speck 30.1 cm out at cos_fwd 0.65, isolated, on the same forward side as the Michel arm and well clear of the muon body line: a detached capture gamma, so kind is both. f_meas shows real measured charge in the arm in U and V with the nearest dead bands 15-20 channels off the stop.

The chain labels it gamma body exclusion, which is its reason for not counting it as a capture gamma, not a claim that it is muon body activity - at cos_fwd -0.12 and 16 cm out it is nowhere near the body line. column40: 172.6 cm chain in four segments, enters 5.7 cm from the y face and the fit ends deep inside the volume, 64.2 cm from the nearest (x) face and 133 cm from the z wall, so containment is not in doubt. The profile is the overshoot case. It sits on a 4.5-5.5e4 plateau from s=100 in to s=20, then climbs along the shape of the muon curve to 8.2-8.5e4 at s=10-13 and 9.4e4, 9.9e4, 1.01e5 and 1.05e5 at s=11-16 - a clean factor-two Bragg rise - and then collapses: 7.4e4 at s=9, 6.1e4 at s=7, 2.7e4 at s=6, a run of near-zero fit points from s=1-5 that I ignore as unmeasured, and 1.85e4 and 2.15e4 at the last point. That is a sustained fall to about 0.4 of the track own MIP plateau over the final 9 cm, exactly where a muon at its Bragg peak should be highest, and it coincides with a whole fitted segment: 58001 is 19 points over 10.9 cm at a mean 18555 e/cm against 48831, 42323 and 44642 for the other three. The three azimuths show why - past the black end-of-cloud marker the amber fit band runs on alone for about 10 cm to the star with no point-cloud halo beside it, and the cropped U panels of f_meas show the measured charge stopping where that band starts, with measured matching predicted and the dead bands far away. So I moved the pin to the 58001 / 58003 junction at 9.65 cm and tagged 58001 michel per the overshoot rule; the true stop is at the peak. The only other object is a 2-point 0.2 cm speck 50 cm out, delta / other. What makes this medium rather than high: the bridged stretch is faint enough that it could equally be read as the fit running past the muon end into a sparse tail with no decay electron at all, which would make it STM_ONLY with kind none.

column40: 154 cm chain entering 0.3 cm from the z face and stopping 21.0 cm from the x (anode) face, inside the volume. The Bragg rise is clean and follows the reference curve the whole way: 5.5-6.5e4 plateau beyond s=15, 7-8e4 at s=8-11, 8.7-9.5e4 at s=4-6, 1.1-1.15e5 at s=2-3 and a top pair at 1.37-1.40e5 within the last 1.5 cm, and the range, dQ/dx and MCS momenta agree at 461/466/444 MeV/c with ambiguity 0.32. I ran the undershoot check explicitly, because the chain does offer a forward piece as the Michel: 75001, 9 points over 5.1 cm at a 45 degree kink from the stop vertex. It fails the undershoot on the load-bearing clause, which is charge - its mean is 43491 e/cm, below the 6.7e4 MIP line, and on the panel its points scatter between 1.9e4 and 1.03e5 with most of them at 2-3.5e4, whereas the undershoot piece is a 1-3 cm stub at 0.9-1.2e5 sitting straight ahead at cos_fwd above 0.85. Here cos_fwd is 0.70 and the piece is 5 cm long. Decisive on top of that, the muon already has its Bragg peak at 1.4e5 on its own last point and a muon cannot have two of those, so an arm leaving that peak at or below MIP is a second particle - the ordinary STM_MICHEL case. Five centimetres and 13.9 MeV is the right scale for a Michel, and the c, d and e azimuths all show it as a distinct blue arm breaking off the star at a visible angle. Past the stop there are also two detached 2-point specks: 214006 at 29.1 cm, cos_fwd 0.41, and 213005 at 48.5 cm, cos_fwd -0.05, both well clear of the muon body and both detached across a clean charge-free gap. Taking their 3-D directions from the stop, they sit 24 and 48 degrees off the Michel arm direction and only 29 degrees from each other, so they are clustered on the decay side rather than scattered around the ring, which the rubric makes gammas - charge is not a criterion for them. Michel plus gammas gives kind both.

That is a clear Bragg rise with no terminal collapse, so the pin stays. Decay topology: 40001, an 11 cm arm with d_min 0, leaves the stop vertex at a clear kink (cos_fwd -0.6; in the three azimuths it bends away from the body at roughly 50-90 deg) and carries 4-10e4, i.e. plateau to twice plateau. The muon is already at its Bragg peak, so this arm is a second particle, and 11 cm is the right range for a Michel electron. 159004 (1.4 cm, 10 cm out) sits at the arm far end: michel, within the ~10 cm radius. 160005 and 161006 are tiny 2-point specks 25 and 36 cm out, about 15 and 26 cm off the body line, lying on the same side as the Michel arm (lower-left in the d frame): gamma. C155, C156 and C157 have no charge value, and their centroids are at x=-370 to -388, beyond the bottom anode: degenerate rows, delta / other. f_meas: the track own charge ends at the stop in all three planes, with no dead band there; the grey below the stop is isolated specks, not the line continuing.

85.8 cm chain entering 0.2 cm from the x face and stopping 19.2 cm inside it. The profile follows the solid muon curve from about 20 cm in: ~5.5e4 plateau out past 40 cm, 6.5-7e4 at 12-18, 8.0-9.0e4 at 3-8 and 1.05e5 and 1.20e5 in the last centimetre and a half, with the maximum at the fit's own last point, so the pin stays put. An arm of three pieces leaves that same point at a large angle -- the chain measures the kink at 102 degrees and puts 23.1 MeV in it -- made of 115007 (5 points, 2.3 cm, 42770 e/cm) touching the stop, then 115008 (9 points, 4.8 cm, 18740) and 115011 (17 points, 9.5 cm, 19662) continuing out to about 16 cm, with all three lying within 3 degrees of the same direction. The three azimuths show it directly: the amber muon body ends at the star and a separate teal-green arm runs off it sideways, and f_meas shows that arm as charge attached to the muon's last point in all three planes. That is a Michel: a muon at its own Bragg peak cannot carry on at three quarters of MIP and then fall to a third of it, and the arm's charge falls as it goes out, which is the ordinary Michel case and not the undershoot trap -- the tip is well below MIP, not the four-to-six times MIP that would make it the muon's own last centimetres. The three far 2-point specks go the other way: 540012 at 22.7 cm and 541013 at 35.4 cm both lie back along the muon body (cos_fwd -0.75 and -0.87, and their directions from the stop are within 30 degrees of the body direction), so they are body activity, and 542014 sits 50 cm out entirely sideways in a direction opposite the Michel arm, which is an unrelated direction round the ring, so all three are delta / other and the kind stays attached rather than both.

column40: 206 cm of chain over a 195 cm chord, entering 0.1 cm from the anode x face at x 339.9 and stopping at (204.7, 10.3, 217.5), which is 80.9 cm from the nearest wall, 135 cm from the anode and 205 cm from the cathode plane, so the stop is deeply contained in every direction. The climb is monotone over 40 cm with only the usual scatter, there is no terminal collapse and no dip in the last few centimetres, so the pin stays on the fit last point, and there is no short high-charge piece past the fit end either, so this is neither the overshoot nor the undershoot case. All three energy estimators agree at 479 MeV by range, 497 by dQ/dx and 453 by MCS with amb 0.02, which is what a genuine stopper of this length should give, and the chain agrees, is_stm 1. Nothing whatever sits past the stop: the object table has only the two chain segments, and the flow reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no unfitted dot clusters and no capture gamma in the ring, which the three azimuths confirm, one clean unbranched track running into the star with empty space beyond. That makes it a stopping muon with no decay activity: STM_ONLY, kind none, both chain segments muon. The only caveat is a grey dead-channel band running immediately beside the track end in the V plane near channel 7200, but a track lost into a dead region would truncate at MIP rather than climb smoothly to twice the plateau, so I do not think it explains the profile.
